# DrivAerML {#sec-drivaerml}

**One car family carries the book's two aerodynamic tasks: the Surface task, where the prediction points are the boundary cells themselves, and the Volume task, where they lie in the flow around the car. At full data ISLA leads GeoTransolver at its recipe width on the surface, ties its parameter match at lower cost, and leads GeoTransolver-volume on interior pressure and velocity.** This chapter follows the layout every dataset chapter shares: the problem and its diversity, what is measured, the standing of the three architectures under their reference configurations, the ladders and controls that belong to this dataset, and what the dataset does not say. The pose and discretization probes run on this dataset are read with their twins on the wings in @sec-invariances (@sec-robustness-density, @sec-training-law, @sec-territories, @sec-pose-contract) and are not repeated here. Protocol: @sec-protocol; the metric is the area-weighted relative L2 in float32 (@sec-metrics); every ratio is baseline ÷ ISLA, above one favoring ISLA.

```{python}
#| label: setup-drivaerml
#| include: false
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
import json, statistics
from pathlib import Path
RES = Path("..") / "results"
J = lambda p: json.load(open(RES / p))
mean = statistics.mean
pct = lambda r: f"{abs(1 - r) * 100:.0f}%"

# ISLA is the reference configuration (384 wide, 12 layers, 256 slices, cosine routing, fused kernel, 5e-4), scored by
# the fleet scorer and reduced in results/ref_surface_2026-09-23.json; the training-car ladder below 435 cars is the
# re-run of the same rungs (results/refboard_ladder_2026-09-23.json); the baseline rows are the released
# GeoTransolver and Transolver lanes of the reporting protocol.
REF = J("ref_surface_2026-09-23.json")["summary"]
ref_seeds = lambda k, f="pressure_l2": REF[k]["fields"][f]["seeds"]
RB = J("refboard_ladder_2026-09-23.json"); RBS = RB["summary"]; RBX = RB["learning_curve_exponents"]
P2 = J("p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json")
def ladder_rung(n):
    gt = {"1e-3": RBS[f"gt256|n{n}"], "3e-3": RBS[f"gt256_lr3e3|n{n}"]}
    glab = min(gt, key=lambda k: gt[k]["mean"])
    return dict(isla=RBS[f"isla_r1|n{n}"]["seeds"], gt=gt[glab]["seeds"], gt_rate=glab, t=RBS[f"transolver256|n{n}"]["seeds"])
A = P2["arms"]
gt435 = {"1e-3": A["gt_unit_lr1e3"], "3e-3": A["gt_unit_lr3e3"]}
g435lab = min(gt435, key=lambda k: gt435[k]["pressure_mean"])
runs = lambda a: [v["pressure_l2"] for v in a["per_run"].values()]
CARS = {n: ladder_rung(n) for n in (27, 54, 109, 218)}
CARS[435] = dict(isla=ref_seeds("isla_r1|dr435"), gt=runs(gt435[g435lab]), gt_rate=g435lab, t=runs(A["transolver_unit_lr3e3"]))
car_ratio = {n: (mean(r["gt"]) / mean(r["isla"]), mean(r["t"]) / mean(r["isla"])) for n, r in CARS.items()}
# the parameter-matched GeoTransolver-512, the 24-layer depth variant and the rate control, all at 435 cars; step time
# and memory of every configuration at 200,000 tokens from the reference cost sweep
GT512 = ref_seeds("gt_w512|dr435"); R2 = ref_seeds("isla_r2|dr435"); R1_LR = ref_seeds("isla_r1_lr1e3|dr435")
CS = {r["arm"]: r for r in J("cost_sweep_ref_gb300_bf16_2026-09-22.json")["runs"] if r["tokens"] == 200000 and r["status"] == "ok"}
COST = {k: (statistics.median(CS[a]["step_ms"]), CS[a]["peak_allocated_gib"]) for k, a in
        (("isla", "isla_ref_r1_384x12_cos_fused"), ("r2", "isla_ref_r2_384x24_cos_fused"), ("gt", "geotransolver_256"),
         ("gt512", "geotransolver_512"), ("t", "transolver_256"))}
ratio = lambda a, b, i: COST[a][i] / COST[b][i]   # cost ratios are baseline ÷ ISLA, two decimals everywhere
PC = J("drivaer435_percase_2026-09-23.json")  # per-car anatomy of the 435-car standing (ISLA against GeoTransolver-512)
# the Volume task: GeoTransolver-volume and ISLA with query tokens
from matplotlib.colors import Normalize
FIELDS = [("pressure_l2", "pressure"), ("velocity_l2", "velocity"), ("nut_l2", "eddy viscosity")]
# ISLA is the reference configuration (384 x 12, cosine routing, 5e-4, `source_total` query mass), scored by the fleet scorer
# on both interior datasets and reduced in results/ref_surface_2026-09-23.json; GeoTransolver-volume is the released baseline
# of the reporting protocol on each dataset.
REF = J("ref_surface_2026-09-23.json")
REFS = REF["summary"]; REFL = REF["lanes"]
def ref_arm(key):
    return {f: dict(mean=REFS[key]["fields"][f]["mean"], seeds=REFS[key]["fields"][f]["seeds"]) for f, _ in FIELDS}
# ISLA's parameter counts on the volume task, from each lane's own config line
lane_params = lambda lane: json.loads(open(RES / f"campaigns_2026-09-22/ref/metrics/{lane}/{lane}/metrics.jsonl").readline())["num_parameters"] / 1e6
ISLA_PARAMS = lane_params("ref_isla_r1_drvol_seed42"); R2_PARAMS = lane_params("ref_isla_r2_drvol_seed42")
# DrivAerML Volume task: GeoTransolver-volume and ISLA with query tokens, 200,000 cells and 200,000 queries per car
RVA = J("ratevol_reduction_2026-09-20.json")["arms"]
GTV = {f: RVA["gt_vol_unit"][f] for f, _ in FIELDS}
ISLAV = ref_arm("isla_r1|drvol"); ISLAV_R2 = ref_arm("isla_r2|drvol")
RATIO = {f: GTV[f]["mean"] / ISLAV[f]["mean"] for f, _ in FIELDS}
PAIRED = {f: [g / i for g, i in zip(GTV[f]["seeds"], ISLAV[f]["seeds"])] for f, _ in FIELDS}
# the interior training-car rungs (54 and 109 cars) of the reference configuration
VOL_RUNGS = {54: ref_arm("isla_r1|drvol_n54"), 109: ref_arm("isla_r1|drvol_n109"), 435: ISLAV}
# AirfRANS (interior task): the same pair on 800 training airfoils, 100,000 queries per case
AF = J("airfrans_reduction_2026-09-22.json"); AFA = AF["arms"]
AFG = {f: AFA["gt_volume_1e-3"][f] for f, _ in FIELDS}
AFI = ref_arm("isla_r1|af"); AFI_R2 = ref_arm("isla_r2|af")
AFR = {f: AFG[f]["mean"] / AFI[f]["mean"] for f, _ in FIELDS}
AFP = {f: [g / i for g, i in zip(AFG[f]["seeds"], AFI[f]["seeds"])] for f, _ in FIELDS}
spread = lambda s: abs(s[0] / s[1] - 1) * 100
lead = lambda r: f"{(r - 1) * 100:.0f}%"
trail = lambda r: f"{(1 - r) * 100:.0f}%"
def standing(r, p):
    """Word a ratio with its paired seeds: a lead or a deficit only when both paired ratios sit on the same side of one."""
    if r > 1.02 and min(p) > 1: return f"leads by {r:.2f}x" if r >= 1.5 else f"leads by {lead(r)}"
    if r < 0.98 and max(p) < 1: return f"trails by {trail(r)}"
    return f"is level (ratio {r:.2f})"
from matplotlib.colors import TwoSlopeNorm
from matplotlib.collections import LineCollection
PF = RES / "problem_figures_2026-09-22"

def load_problem(name):
    """One representative sample of a dataset, reduced for plotting (results/problem_figures_2026-09-22/)."""
    z = np.load(PF / f"{name}.npz"); meta = json.load(open(PF / f"{name}.json"))
    return {k: z[k] for k in z.files}, meta

def bc_segments(ax, pts, cells, kinds, lw=4.0, zorder=3):
    """Draw line cells colored by boundary-condition kind (keys of palette.BC)."""
    segs = pts[cells][:, :, :2]
    ax.add_collection(LineCollection(segs, colors=[BC[k] for k in kinds], linewidths=lw, capstyle="butt", zorder=zorder))

def field_scatter(ax, xy, v, s=3.0, signed=False, vmin=None, vmax=None):
    if signed:
        lim = max(abs(np.nanmin(v)), abs(np.nanmax(v))) if vmin is None else None
        norm = TwoSlopeNorm(vcenter=0.0, vmin=(-lim if vmin is None else vmin), vmax=(lim if vmax is None else vmax))
        return ax.scatter(xy[:, 0], xy[:, 1], c=v, s=s, lw=0, cmap=DIVERGING, norm=norm, rasterized=True)
    return ax.scatter(xy[:, 0], xy[:, 1], c=v, s=s, lw=0, cmap=SEQUENTIAL, vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax, rasterized=True)

def small_colorbar(fig, sc, ax, label, **kw):
    cb = fig.colorbar(sc, ax=ax, fraction=0.035, pad=0.02, **kw); cb.outline.set_visible(False); cb.ax.tick_params(labelsize=8)
    cb.set_label(label, fontsize=8.5)
    return cb

def bc_legend(ax, kinds, loc="lower right", extra=()):
    from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
    handles = [Line2D([], [], color=BC[k], lw=4, label=BC_LABEL[k]) for k in kinds] + list(extra)
    ax.legend(handles=handles, loc=loc, fontsize=8, frameon=True, facecolor="white", edgecolor=BASELINE)

# ---- the three-protocol headline table ----
# The three architectures' reference configurations scored on (i) the native validation mesh, (ii) a uniform point cloud of
# the same budget and (iii) every validation case rotated and translated. Read from results/char/<dataset>.json when that
# artifact exists; until it does the cell prints nothing and the native-mesh table above is the headline. Expected schema:
# {"fields": {key: label}, "protocols": {"native": label, "uniform": label, "posed": label}, "isla_arm": name,
#  "arms": {name: {protocol: {field: {"mean": x, "seeds": [...]}}}}}.
def protocol_table(artifact, label, setting):
    p = RES / "char" / artifact
    if not p.exists():
        return
    C = json.load(open(p)); protos = C["protocols"]; fields = C["fields"]; isla = C["arms"][C["isla_arm"]]
    flab = " / ".join(fields.values())
    hdr = "| configuration | " + " | ".join(f"{pl}: {flab}" for pl in protos.values()) + " |\n|---|" + "---|" * len(protos) + "\n"
    rows = []
    for arm, d in C["arms"].items():
        rows.append(f"| {arm} | " + " | ".join(" / ".join(f"{d[pk][f]['mean']:.4f}" for f in fields) for pk in protos) + " |")
        if arm != C["isla_arm"]:
            rows.append(f"| {arm} ÷ ISLA | " + " | ".join(" / ".join(f"{d[pk][f]['mean'] / isla[pk][f]['mean']:.2f}" for f in fields) for pk in protos) + " |")
    print(hdr + "\n".join(rows) + "\n")
    print(f": {setting}: the three architectures at their reference configurations under three scorings of one instrument, the "
          f"native validation mesh, a uniform point cloud at the same budget, and every validation case rotated and translated; "
          f"fields {flab}; seed means, float32. How to read this: a ratio is baseline ÷ ISLA, above one favoring ISLA; the three "
          f"columns share the checkpoint and differ only in how the validation cases are presented. Data: results/char/{artifact}. "
          f"{{#{label}}}")

```

## The problem: one notchback family in one far field {#sec-benchmarks}

**DrivAerML is 484 parametrically morphed variants of one notchback car, each simulated once in the same far-field flow, so geometry is the only thing that varies and the global inputs are constants.** Every model is fed the vehicle surface alone, the information diet of every published baseline on the dataset. The recipe assigns 435 variants to training and 48 to validation, one validation set shared by both tasks and every experiment. @fig-problem-drivaer shows one validation car with both tasks' fields.

```{python}
#| label: fig-problem-drivaer
#| fig-cap: >

#|   scalar target, seen from the side and from above; the black arrow is the
#|   far-field flow direction, the one global vector input, and the far-field
#|   speed is the same for every car. Bottom: the symmetry plane of the volume
#|   mesh, colored by the speed ratio $|U| / U_\infty$, with the car's outline
#|   in black; the Volume task predicts pressure, velocity and turbulent
#|   viscosity at 200,000 query points drawn from this mesh, whose extent is
#|   printed. What varies per sample is the geometry only. What the model
#|   receives: the surface cells' positions, outward normals and areas, and the
#|   flow direction; the ground plane and the wind-tunnel boundaries are not

ax = axes[0]
depth_scatter(ax, sp[:, [0, 2]], sp[:, 1], cp, s=2.2, cmap=DIVERGING, norm=norm); map_axes(ax)
ax.set_ylabel("z [m]"); ax.set_title("side view: surface pressure coefficient $C_p$, the Surface task's scalar target", fontsize=9.5)

```

**Diversity.** The set is narrow by design. Every case is a morph of one body (the DrivAer notchback) under one far-field condition, so the operator is learned as a function of shape within one family (@sec-parametric): a validation car differs from the training cars in the same parameters they differ in from one another. The far-field direction, the speed and the ground clearance never change, which is why the dataset carries no global scalar ($K = 1$, $S = 0$) and why a lead on it says nothing about a change of family or of regime (@sec-limits-transfer).

### Files, conversion and normalization {#sec-data-drivaer}

**484 parametrically morphed DrivAer notchback variants in one far-field
condition; the boundary is the vehicle surface alone, and the two tasks
read different parts of the same files.** Each case is a `run_<id>`
directory holding a `domain_*.pdmsh` with the vehicle boundary
(`boundaries.vehicle`, triangles), the tetrahedral volume mesh with its
point fields, the watertight `*_single_solid.stl.pmsh` of the body, and
`global_data` with the far-field conditions `U_inf` (38.89 m/s along $x$),
`rho_inf`, `p_inf` (zero: the pressure is gauge), `nu` and `L_ref` (5 m).
The reader divides coordinates by `L_ref`, so a car spans about one unit.
The sample car in @tbl-data-samples has 17.0 million surface cells and
160 million volume points; @sec-interior-task states the volume range across
cars as 150 to 166 million.

- **Surface task.** The recipe reads the boundary tensordict directly
  (`run_*/*.pdmsh/_tensordict/boundaries/vehicle`). Fields
  `pMeanTrim` and `wallShearStressMeanTrim` (time-averaged) are
  nondimensionalized from the case's own `global_data`
  (`NonDimensionalizeByMetadata`: pressure by the far-field dynamic
  pressure, stress likewise) and renamed `pressure` and `wss`; `wss` is
  further scaled by a fixed standard deviation (0.00313). Normals are
  recomputed from the faces after centering (`ComputeSurfaceNormals`);
  the cell subsample and `DropDegenerateCells` follow; `MeshToDomainMesh`
  puts the prediction points at the cell centroids. `U_inf_dir` is written
  from `U_inf` before centering so the augmentation block (axis-aligned
  rotations about $z$, used by the baselines' pose lanes only) rotates it
  with the geometry.
- **Volume task.** `DomainMeshReader` on `run_*/domain_*.pdmsh` with the
  interior as a point cloud (tetrahedral topology dropped), the vehicle
  boundary subsampled by cells, and the STL as an extra boundary from
  which `ComputeSDFFromBoundary` writes `sdf` and `sdf_normals` at the
  query points (pseudo-normal sign, exact on the watertight STL) before
  the STL is dropped. `UMeanTrim`, `pMeanTrim`, `nutMeanTrim` become
  `velocity` (by $|U_\infty|$), `pressure` (by the dynamic pressure) and
  `nut` (standardized with mean 4.8e-4 and standard deviation 9.4e-4,
  m²/s).
- **What is not an input.** The ground plane and the wind-tunnel
  boundaries are present in the source files and are read by no
  configuration in the book; every model sees the vehicle surface only.
- **Splits.** One validation set of 48 cars, fixed across every
  experiment and shared by the two tasks; 435 training cars, with nested
  rungs of 27, 54, 109 and 218 for the data-efficiency ladder
  (@sec-car-ladder); one variant is in neither set. The
  sampling-density and pose probes evaluate the same 48 cars with
  transformed inputs (@sec-discretization-evidence).
- **License.** The dataset is distributed by its authors under their own
  terms; this program's artifacts do not restate them.

## What is measured {#sec-drivaerml-measured}

### The Surface task {#sec-surface}

**The Surface task predicts pressure and wall shear at the sampled boundary cells of a car it has not seen.** The reporting protocol samples the recipe's default of 200,000 surface cells per case per step, trains for 500 epochs with two seeds, each architecture at its own best learning rate, and scores the area-weighted relative L2 of surface pressure in float32 over the 48 validation cars (@sec-protocol, @sec-metrics). The surface instrument is pressure and wall shear on those 48 cars at 200,000 cells, and it is never widened (@sec-review-instrument).

### The Volume task: boundary to interior {#sec-interior}

A surrogate that returns only wall pressure answers one engineering
question, the forces. One that returns the field in the domain answers the
rest: wake structure, cooling-flow paths, where separation begins. The task
here is the second in its strictest form: predict the fields inside the
domain from the boundary alone. @fig-interior-task shows it on the running
example. ISLA is held to that form. GeoTransolver's volume configuration is
not. It never sees the surface sample. Instead, at every interior point it
takes the signed distance to the full-resolution boundary and its
gradient, which is the boundary information in a different, denser form.

```{python}
#| label: fig-interior-task
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The boundary-to-interior task on the airfoil. Inputs: the sampled
#|   boundary (black dots with normals, as in the surface task) and a set of
#|   interior query points (aqua). Target: the pressure coefficient at the
#|   query points, shown here as the exact potential-flow field the queries
#|   sample. How to read this: the model sees the boundary and the query
#|   positions and must produce the field at the aqua points; on DrivAerML
#|   the field is a RANS solution with a separated wake, for which no closed
#|   form exists, and each query also carries its signed distance to the
#|   wall. It does not show any model's prediction.
#| code-fold: true
Jk = joukowski(n_cells=50)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.0, 3.9))
clean_axes(ax); ax.set_xlim(-2.6, 2.8); ax.set_ylim(-1.5, 1.6)
xs = np.linspace(-2.6, 2.8, 301); ys = np.linspace(-1.5, 1.6, 181)
X, Y = np.meshgrid(xs, ys); Z = X + 1j * Y
cp = Jk["cp_field"](Z)
c0 = complex(-0.08, 0.08); a0 = abs(1 - c0)
inside = (np.abs((Z + np.sqrt(Z * Z - 4 + 0j)) / 2 - c0) < a0 + 1e-9) & (np.abs((Z - np.sqrt(Z * Z - 4 + 0j)) / 2 - c0) < a0 + 1e-9)
cp = np.where(inside, np.nan, np.clip(cp, -1.6, 1.0))
norm = Normalize(-1.6, 1.0)
ax.pcolormesh(X, Y, cp, cmap=DIVERGING, norm=norm, shading="auto", alpha=0.6, rasterized=True)
ax.fill(Jk["xy"][:, 0], Jk["xy"][:, 1], color="white", zorder=2)
ax.plot(Jk["xy"][:, 0], Jk["xy"][:, 1], color=INK, lw=1.4, zorder=3)
ax.plot(Jk["mid"][:, 0], Jk["mid"][:, 1], "o", ms=3, color=INK, zorder=4)
rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
q = np.stack([rng.uniform(-2.4, 2.6, 400), rng.uniform(-1.3, 1.4, 400)], axis=1)
qz = q[:, 0] + 1j * q[:, 1]
zeta = (qz + np.sqrt(qz * qz - 4 + 0j)) / 2
keep = np.abs(zeta - c0) > a0 * 1.06
q = q[keep][:140]
ax.plot(q[:, 0], q[:, 1], "o", ms=4, mfc=AQUA, mec="white", mew=0.6, zorder=5)
ax.text(-2.5, 1.35, "input: boundary sample (black), interior query points (aqua)", fontsize=9.5, color=INK)
ax.text(-2.5, -1.4, "target: the field at the query points (color: exact $C_p$)", fontsize=9.5, color=INK2)
sm = plt.cm.ScalarMappable(norm=norm, cmap=DIVERGING); sm.set_array([])
cb = fig.colorbar(sm, ax=ax, fraction=0.03, pad=0.02); cb.set_label("pressure coefficient $C_p$ [–]", color=INK2)
plt.show()
```

#### The data, the metric and what each architecture receives {#sec-interior-task}

**Data.** The DrivAerML Volume task (@sec-benchmarks): the 435-car training
split and the 48-car validation split used for every DrivAerML comparison
in the book. Each car contributes a sample of the vehicle boundary (cell
centroids, unit normals, cell areas as measure weights) and a sample of
200,000 interior query points drawn from the CFD volume mesh, bit-identical
across every trained run. The volume mesh holds 150 to 166 million points
per car, so even this sample covers about $10^{-3}$ of it and is
overwhelmingly near the wall. Targets are the static pressure, the three
velocity components and the turbulent eddy viscosity $\nu_t$.

**Metric.** For one car and one field $f$ the relative L2 error is
$\lVert \hat f - f\rVert_2 / \lVert f\rVert_2$ over the query points,
with $f$ in training normalization: pressure as $C_p$, velocity as
$U/|U_\infty|$ with the far-field mean included (Frobenius norm over the
components), and eddy viscosity standardized to zero mean and unit scale
*before* scoring. The viscosity denominator is therefore the norm of a
mean-subtracted field, so an eddy-viscosity value of 0.10 is not a 10% error
in physical $\nu_t$: orderings under this metric stand, but the number is
not a physical percentage. The reported value is the arithmetic mean over
the 48 cars (@sec-metrics).

**Protocol.** @sec-protocol, with 200,000 boundary cells and 200,000
interior queries per car. GeoTransolver-volume trains at 1e-3 and ISLA at
the reference configuration's 5e-4. Both are scored in float32 at the
training query count. The arms are not resource-matched and do not receive
the same inputs. GeoTransolver-volume has 27.6M parameters: the surface
configuration's 12-layer, 256-wide backbone plus ball-query local features
over neighboring interior points at six radii. Its tokens are the interior
points only, and each carries its coordinates, the signed distance to the
full-resolution surface and that distance's gradient. Fed the physical
far-field velocity vector instead of the unit direction, it changes by under
2% on every field, so the interior ordering does not depend on the
input-scale rule of @sec-part-baseline. ISLA with query tokens is the
reference configuration (384 wide, 12 layers,
`{python} f"{ISLA_PARAMS:.1f}M"` parameters,
`{python} f"{ISLA_PARAMS / 27.6:.2f}x"` GeoTransolver-volume's),
and its per-slice geometry spans surface and query tokens together. The
parameter difference is stated here once. It could buy accuracy, so the
interior ratios are read as standings of the two configurations as
shipped, not as a matched-capacity comparison.

#### How each architecture treats an interior point

| architecture | what an interior point is | what it knows about the geometry | does the prediction at a point depend on the other points requested |
|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver-volume | an interacting token, routed to slices with the other interior points of the request | its signed distance to the wall and the nearest wall normal; ball-query features over neighboring interior points at six radii; no surface tokens | yes |
| ISLA with query tokens | an interacting token in the encoder alongside the surface tokens, with a learned type embedding and routing weight | the relational invariants of its position against the surface anchors, plus the wall normal and the signed distance as a query scalar | yes |

#### ISLA with query tokens {#sec-interior-query-tokens}

ISLA with query tokens admits the queries into the encoder as tokens. Each
query is seeded exactly as a boundary token is, from the invariants of its
position, its wall normal and the global direction, plus a learned type
embedding and the signed distance as a query scalar. In every lane of this
chapter the queries also carry the dataset's full-mesh signed-distance
field and its gradient as inputs; the class derives a direction and a
distance from the boundary sample itself, and the model's own
geometry is computed regardless (@sec-arch-modes). Each query enters the
measure-weighted routing with a learned weight relative to the surface
measure. The twelve slice layers run over surface and query tokens together,
and the heads read the query tokens. Every invariant is a function of
relative geometry, so rotation and translation covariance hold by
construction (@sec-isla-contracts). What is given up is query independence:
a query's prediction depends on the other queries in the request. The
queries' total routing weight is a learned fraction of the total boundary
measure, split equally over them, so re-representing the same surface at
another refinement leaves the routing unchanged (measure-rescale
invariant). Nothing else changes: the reference configuration's
width, depth and slice count, the surface configuration's
hyperparameters, no local features.

```{python}
      "ratio after each ISLA cell is GeoTransolver-volume ÷ ISLA (above 1 favors ISLA); the paired row divides seed by seed. How to read "
      "this: the arms are not resource-matched and do not receive the same inputs (@sec-interior-task); ISLA is the reference "
      "configuration (@sec-interior-query-tokens), and the last row is the depth variant the reference "
      "selection rejected. The AirfRANS twin of "
      "this table is @tbl-interior-airfrans. Data: results/ratevol_reduction_2026-09-20.json "

```

Two ingredient orderings sit behind the row. Both were measured at the
exploration budget of 10,000 cells and queries and are stated as orderings
only. First, admitting the queries as interacting tokens, rather than
decoding them read-only from the encoder's final states, closes most of
ISLA's gap to GeoTransolver-volume on pressure, without the signed distance
and without extra parameters. Second, the signed distance closes most of
the rest, most on velocity, and that is what turns the velocity standing
into a lead. A true wall normal at the query (the signed-distance gradient)
is better information than a covariant blend of anchor normals, on pressure
by a wide margin. One caution applies to any per-band reading of these
fields. Far from the body the true $C_p$ has an RMS two orders of magnitude
below the near-wall value, so far-band pressure relative L2 is
ill-conditioned for every architecture. The velocity error, whose
denominator is the far-field speed, is the well-conditioned view of the far
field.

### Dependence on the query cloud {#sec-interior-companion}

**The interacting configuration's answer at a point depends on how many
other points are asked for with it, so a surrogate built from it is
queried in batches of at least the training count** (@sec-using-checkpoint).
Because the queries route through the same slices as the surface, a
prediction at one point is a function of the whole request. Two instruments establish the
rule at the exploration budget. A checkpoint trained at a fixed query count
and scored at a fifth of it loses more on every field than either margin
against GeoTransolver-volume, while twice the count gains a little. And
fixed sentinel points predicted alone and with growing companion sets move
with the request size, most for eddy viscosity and least for pressure
(results/qcount_reduction_2026-09-11.json,
results/isla_qt_companion_dependence_2026-09-08.json). Training over a
range of counts reduces the dependence and does not remove it, so
query-count consistency is an architectural question. The queries' routing
mass, a learned fraction of the total boundary measure split over the
request, removes the count-scaling of the query weight by construction
(@sec-isla-contracts). The dependence through the shared slices remains. A
read-only decoder whose predictions are exactly query-independent is
several times less accurate on every interior field, which is why the class
offers none (@sec-arch-passive-decoder, @sec-principled-decisions).

### What does not work on the interior {#sec-interior-negatives}

**Two mechanisms tested as ways to give ISLA interior context or an
interior prior, other than admitting the queries themselves as tokens,
both fail.** Latent volume tokens placed covariantly along the anchor
normals (769 tokens entering the routing as interacting tokens, with the
requested queries decoded read-only from the result) are worse on every
field than the same decode without them
(results/v0_lvt_reduction_2026-09-07.json). An exact
boundary-integral prior is the wrong prior for separated flow. On the 45 of
48 DrivAerML validation cars whose remesh passes a watertightness check,
exact inviscid potential flow evaluated at the recipe's surface points has a
measure-weighted relative L2 of 4.8 against the CFD pressure, where
predicting zero scores 1.00. The reason is that most of a DrivAerML surface
carries the separated-base pressure deficit that inviscid flow cannot
produce. The learned-density decoder built on those kernels is about ten
times less accurate than GeoTransolver-volume on interior pressure on the
DrivAerML Volume task, and its far-field output decays to identically zero.
ISLA therefore evaluates no exact boundary-integral kernels and places no
latent tokens off the surface.

### Pose and discretization {#sec-drivaerml-invariances}

On this dataset the inference-draw probe, the convergence benchmark, the training-law swap, the slice-territory probe and the posed evaluation are all run at 435 cars, and they are read beside their HiLiftAeroML twins in @sec-discretization-evidence; the cell-count, width and depth ladders at 435 cars are @sec-capacity.

## What this dataset does not say {#sec-interior-open}

**The surface lead is one dataset, one task and one metric, measured in distribution, and the interior lead is measured at the training query count by two models that are neither resource-matched nor input-matched.** Nothing here speaks to a change of vehicle family, of far-field condition or of flow regime, because none varies in the set (@sec-limits-transfer, @sec-limits-regime). The surface parity with GeoTransolver-512 is a statement about cost, not accuracy (@sec-limits-in-distribution). The interior standing's scope, and the third seeds and baseline rungs that would settle its open parts, are in @sec-limits-interior. The wing standings, where both baselines lead, are @sec-hilift.
